note: WAEC/NECO Chemistry Paper 1, round 1: full SSCE syllabus - matter, atomic structure, periodicity, bonding, mole concept and stoichiometry, gas laws, solutions, water, electrolysis, rates and equilibrium, acids/bases/salts, redox, metals, non-metals, organic chemistry and separation techniques. All calculations machine-verified (molar volume 22.4 dm3 at s.t.p., F = 96,500 C).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Diffusion is the movement of particles
questions.A: from a region of lower concentration to a higher one
questions.B: from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration
questions.D: that stops when a gas is cooled
questions.explanation: Particles spread down their concentration gradient until evenly distributed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the diffusion of hydrogen chloride and ammonia along a tube, the white ring of ammonium chloride forms nearer the hydrogen chloride end because
questions.B: hydrogen chloride is lighter and diffuses faster
questions.C: ammonia is lighter and diffuses faster
questions.explanation: Ammonia (M = 17) travels further in the same time than the heavier HCl (M = 36.5).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The random movement of tiny pollen grains in water seen under a microscope is called
questions.explanation: Brownian motion is caused by water molecules continually hitting the grains.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which state of matter are the particles held in fixed positions, only vibrating about them?
questions.explanation: Strong forces hold solid particles in a fixed lattice, so they only vibrate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The direct change of a solid into vapour on heating is called
questions.explanation: Solids like iodine and naphthalene sublime straight to vapour on heating.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Evaporation of a liquid in an open dish causes cooling because
questions.B: the dish absorbs heat from the liquid
questions.C: new molecules are formed in the vapour
questions.D: the most energetic molecules escape from the surface
questions.explanation: Only the fastest molecules leave, so the average kinetic energy left behind falls.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The nucleus of an atom contains
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons sit in the nucleus; electrons occupy shells around it.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The atomic number of an element equals the number of
questions.explanation: Atomic number is defined by the proton count and fixes the element's identity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An atom of sodium has mass number 23 and atomic number 11. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many electrons are present in the chloride ion, Cl⁻? (Chlorine's atomic number is 17.)
questions.explanation: The negative charge means one extra electron: 17 + 1 = 18.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ in neutron number, so their mass numbers differ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine exists as 75% of the isotope of mass 35 and 25% of the isotope of mass 37. Its relative atomic mass is

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The electron configuration of an atom of potassium (atomic number 19) is
questions.explanation: Potassium fills the shells 2 then 8 then 8, leaving one electron in the fourth shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An atom with the electron configuration 2, 8, 8 belongs to which group of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: A complete outer shell of eight electrons makes it a noble gas like argon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The maximum number of electrons that can occupy the shell with n = 3 is
questions.explanation: The capacity is 2n² = 2 × 3² = 18 electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element X has 13 protons. The formula of its most common ion is
questions.explanation: With configuration 2, 8, 3, atom X (aluminium) loses three electrons to gain a stable shell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The elements in Group 1 of the periodic table are known collectively as the
questions.explanation: Lithium, sodium and potassium are the soft, reactive alkali metals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which group contains elements that are monatomic and very unreactive gases?
questions.explanation: Noble gases have complete outer shells, so they rarely react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature. Iodine, the element below it, is a
questions.explanation: Down Group 7 the states rise from gas (F₂, Cl₂) to liquid (Br₂) to solid (I₂).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Sodium is stored under oil in the laboratory because it
questions.B: is a very soft metal that crumbles
questions.C: reacts vigorously with air and water
questions.explanation: The oil keeps air and moisture away from the very reactive metal surface.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Going down Group 1 from lithium to potassium, the reactivity of the metals
questions.A: increases because the nucleus attracts more
questions.B: decreases because the atoms get smaller
questions.D: increases because the outer electron is lost more easily
questions.explanation: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and lost more readily down the group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Going down Group 7 from chlorine to iodine, the reactivity of the halogens
questions.explanation: The incoming electron is gained less easily as the atoms get larger.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of electron shells in an atom tells you its
questions.explanation: Elements in the same period have the same number of occupied shells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Copper(II) salts are usually blue in colour. This is a property typical of
questions.explanation: Coloured compounds and variable oxidation states are classic transition-metal features.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The family name for the elements in Group 7 is the
questions.explanation: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine are the halogen family.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element with atomic number 12 belongs to
questions.explanation: Magnesium is 2, 8, 2: two outer electrons (Group 2) in three shells (Period 3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond formed when sodium reacts with chlorine is
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, giving Na⁺ and Cl⁻ held by electrostatic force.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A covalent bond involves the sharing of
questions.A: electrons free to move through a lattice
questions.B: a pair of electrons between two atoms
questions.explanation: Each bonded atom contributes one electron to the shared pair.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺, one of the N–H bonds is formed by a lone pair donated by nitrogen. This bond is described as
questions.explanation: Both shared electrons come from one atom, so the bond is dative (coordinate) covalent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Metals are good conductors of electricity because they
questions.explanation: The delocalised outer electrons drift when a potential difference is applied.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which property is typical of ionic compounds?
questions.A: They have very low boiling points
questions.B: They conduct when molten or in solution
questions.C: They are usually gases at room temperature
questions.D: They dissolve easily in petrol and kerosene
questions.explanation: Strong electrostatic forces give high melting points; melted or dissolved ions carry charge.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Simple molecular covalent substances have low melting points because
questions.B: the covalent bonds inside molecules are weak
questions.C: only weak intermolecular forces exist between the molecules
questions.explanation: Melting separates molecules, overcoming weak forces, not the strong covalent bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not because graphite
questions.D: has free electrons between its layers
questions.explanation: Each carbon in graphite uses three bonds, leaving delocalised electrons that conduct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Diamond is extremely hard because
questions.A: its atoms are held together by ionic bonds
questions.B: each carbon bonds to four others in a network
questions.D: its molecules form very long chains
questions.explanation: The three-dimensional network of strong covalent bonds makes diamond very hard.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The formation of Mg²⁺ from a magnesium atom involves
questions.explanation: Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its two outer electrons to reach a stable arrangement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Water has an unusually high boiling point for such a small molecule because of
questions.C: its covalent bonds inside the molecule
questions.explanation: Strong hydrogen bonds between water molecules need extra energy to break.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which pair of elements would form a compound by electron transfer?
questions.explanation: A metal reacting with a non-metal transfers electrons to form ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The bond that holds a pair of chlorine atoms together in a chlorine molecule is
questions.explanation: The two chlorine atoms share one pair of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: One mole of any substance contains
questions.explanation: The Avogadro constant is 6.02 × 10²³ particles per mole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many moles are present in 8 g of oxygen gas, O₂? (O = 16.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many moles are present in 11 g of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What volume does 0.25 mol of a gas occupy at s.t.p.? (Molar volume = 22.4 dm³.)
questions.explanation: V = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 dm³ at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many molecules are present in 0.5 mol of ammonia gas?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the mass of 0.2 mol of sodium hydroxide? (Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1.)
questions.explanation: M(NaOH) = 40, so mass = 0.2 × 40 = 8 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the concentration of a solution containing 3.65 g of hydrogen chloride in 500 cm³ of solution.
questions.explanation: n = 3.65 ÷ 36.5 = 0.1 mol in 0.5 dm³, so c = 0.2 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 25.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid exactly neutralises 20.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution. The concentration of the alkali is
questions.explanation: For the 1:1 reaction, C(NaOH) = (0.1 × 25) ÷ 20 = 0.125 mol/dm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What mass of calcium oxide is obtained by heating 50 g of calcium carbonate? (CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56.)
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, so 50 g gives 50 × 56/100 = 28 g of CaO.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, what mass of oxygen is needed to burn 8 g of hydrogen completely?
questions.explanation: n(H₂) = 4 mol, needing 2 mol of O₂ = 64 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonia, NH₃? (N = 14, H = 1.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of water in Na₂CO₃·10H₂O? (Na₂CO₃ = 106, H₂O = 18.)
questions.explanation: Ten waters weigh 180 out of 286, giving (180 ÷ 286) × 100 = 63.0%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A hydrocarbon contains 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass. Its empirical formula is
questions.explanation: Dividing by atomic masses gives 7.14 : 14.3, which simplifies to 1 : 2, so CH₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 20 g of an impure sample of calcium carbonate gives 2.24 dm³ of carbon dioxide at s.t.p. The percentage purity of the sample is
questions.explanation: n(CO₂) = 0.1 mol, so 10 g of pure CaCO₃ reacted: (10 ÷ 20) × 100 = 50%.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What mass of copper is deposited when a current is passed through copper(II) sulphate solution for long enough to transfer 0.4 mol of electrons? (Cu = 64.)
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ needs 2 electrons per atom, so 0.2 mol Cu = 12.8 g is deposited.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas occupies 200 cm³ at a pressure of 750 mmHg. What is its volume at 760 mmHg, at the same temperature?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law, V₂ = (750 × 200) ÷ 760 = 197.4 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas occupies 300 cm³ at 27°C. What is its volume at 57°C, at the same pressure?
questions.explanation: Charles' law with kelvin: V₂ = 300 × 330/300 = 330 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In gas law calculations, temperatures must be converted to
questions.explanation: Adding 273 to the Celsius reading gives the kelvin temperature the laws require.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Express 25°C in kelvin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at 300 K and 600 cm³ is heated to 450 K at constant pressure. Its new volume is
questions.explanation: V/T is constant, so V₂ = 600 × 450/300 = 900 cm³.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Gases can be compressed easily because
questions.explanation: The large spaces between gas particles allow them to be pushed closer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a sugar solution, the sugar is the
questions.explanation: The substance dissolved is the solute; the liquid doing the dissolving is the solvent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution that cannot dissolve any more solute at a given temperature is described as
questions.explanation: At saturation the dissolved solute is in equilibrium with the undissolved solid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 5 g of potassium nitrate dissolves in 25 g of water at 20°C. The solubility of potassium nitrate at that temperature is
questions.explanation: Solubility = (5 ÷ 25) × 100 = 20 g of salt per 100 g of water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of a solution made by dissolving 5 g of salt in 95 g of water?
questions.explanation: Percentage = (5 ÷ (5 + 95)) × 100 = 5% of the solution mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Two liquids that mix completely in all proportions, like ethanol and water, are said to be
questions.explanation: Miscible liquids form a single homogeneous layer when mixed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oil and water form two layers on mixing. The best apparatus for separating them is the
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids separate into layers that can be run off through a tap.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A suspension differs from a true solution because a suspension
questions.A: contains no solvent at all in the mixture
questions.B: is always completely colourless to the eye
questions.C: cannot be filtered by ordinary filter paper
questions.D: contains particles that settle out on standing
questions.explanation: Suspension particles are large enough to scatter light and settle on standing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Increasing the temperature usually increases the solubility of a solid solute because
questions.A: the solute evaporates away before dissolving
questions.B: particles move faster and separate more easily
questions.D: the solute particles become larger overall
questions.explanation: Higher kinetic energy helps solvent particles break solute particles apart.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When acidified water is electrolysed, hydrogen and oxygen are collected in the volume ratio
questions.explanation: Water contains twice as many hydrogen atoms, so twice the volume of hydrogen forms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical test for water uses anhydrous copper(II) sulphate, which changes from white to
questions.explanation: Anhydrous CuSO₄ turns blue as it takes up water of crystallisation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Temporary hardness of water is caused mainly by dissolved
questions.explanation: Hydrogencarbonates of calcium and magnesium cause hardness that boiling removes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hardness that cannot be removed by boiling is called permanent hardness. It can be removed by adding
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate precipitates the calcium ions, softening the water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hard water wastes soap because
questions.B: hard water is heavier than soft water
questions.C: soap dissolves better in hard water
questions.D: the calcium salts react with soap to form scum
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium ions form an insoluble scum instead of lather.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In municipal water treatment, alum (aluminium sulphate) is added to
questions.A: kill all the bacteria in the raw water
questions.B: make fine suspended particles clump together
questions.C: soften the hard water in the tank
questions.D: add fluoride ions to the water
questions.explanation: Alum coagulates suspended mud into flocs that settle or are filtered out.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine is added near the end of municipal water treatment in order to
questions.explanation: Chlorination disinfects the supply, making the water safe to drink.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An electrolyte is a substance that
questions.A: dissolves in every liquid it meets
questions.B: conducts electricity as a solid metal
questions.C: never conducts electricity in any state
questions.D: conducts electricity when molten or dissolved
questions.explanation: Electrolytes are ionic substances whose ions become mobile on melting or dissolving.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In electrolysis, oxidation occurs at the
questions.explanation: The anode is the positive electrode where electrons are removed (oxidation).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When molten sodium chloride is electrolysed, the product at the cathode is
questions.explanation: Sodium ions migrate to the cathode and gain electrons to form sodium metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When concentrated sodium chloride solution is electrolysed using carbon electrodes, the gas produced at the anode is
questions.explanation: Chloride ions are discharged in preference to hydroxide ions in concentrated brine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When DILUTE sodium chloride solution is electrolysed, the gas produced at the anode is
questions.explanation: In dilute solution hydroxide ions are discharged in preference to chloride ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When copper(II) sulphate solution is electrolysed with carbon electrodes, the cathode becomes coated with
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ ions are discharged at the cathode as copper metal, and the blue colour fades.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the industrial purification of copper by electrolysis, the impure copper is made the
questions.explanation: Impure copper dissolves from the anode while pure copper deposits on the cathode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In silver plating a spoon by electrolysis, the spoon is made the
questions.explanation: Metal objects to be plated are always the cathode, where the metal deposits.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What quantity of electricity in coulombs is carried by a current of 2 A flowing for 965 s?

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many faradays of electricity are needed to deposit one mole of aluminium from molten alumina?
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ needs three electrons per ion, so three faradays deposit one mole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: A reaction that gives out heat to the surroundings is
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions raise the temperature of the surroundings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: Dissolving ammonium chloride in water causes the container to feel cold. The change is
questions.explanation: Heat is absorbed from the surroundings, so the solution and vessel cool down.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: Powdered marble reacts faster with dilute acid than marble chips because the powder
questions.A: absorbs more water from the acid
questions.B: is chemically purer than the chips
questions.C: is lighter in total mass than chips
questions.D: has a larger total surface area exposed
questions.explanation: More surface is exposed, so more collisions happen per second.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: Increasing the temperature increases the rate of a reaction mainly because
questions.A: the activation energy of reaction falls
questions.B: collisions become more frequent and energetic
questions.explanation: Hotter particles collide more often and more of them exceed the activation energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by
questions.D: being used up in the reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst offers an easier pathway; it is unchanged at the end.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: The minimum energy reacting particles must have for a collision to succeed is the
questions.explanation: Collisions below the activation energy simply bounce apart.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: Manganese(IV) oxide speeds up the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. After the reaction, the MnO₂
questions.explanation: Catalysts are recovered unchanged, which is why only a little is needed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Energy Changes and Rates of Reaction
questions.q: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because
questions.B: the water boils at a lower temperature
questions.C: the higher pressure raises the boiling point of water
questions.D: the food is under less pressure
questions.explanation: Water boils above 100°C inside, so cooking proceeds at a hotter temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction
questions.B: is greater than the backward rate
questions.D: equals the rate of the backward reaction
questions.explanation: Both reactions continue at equal speeds, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Haber process, N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) + heat. Which change increases the yield of ammonia?
questions.explanation: Four gas moles become two, so high pressure shifts the equilibrium to the right.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Haber process, the catalyst used is
questions.explanation: Finely divided iron catalyses the formation of ammonia.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The Contact process for making sulphur trioxide uses which catalyst?
questions.explanation: V₂O₅ catalyses SO₂ + ½O₂ → SO₃ in the Contact process.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Compromise conditions of about 450°C are used in the Haber process because
questions.A: 450°C is the cheapest temperature for fuel
questions.B: a low temperature is too slow though it favours yield
questions.C: iron only works well at exactly 450°C
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is exothermic, so high temperature cuts yield but low temperature is too slow.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Adding a catalyst to a system at equilibrium
questions.A: increases the final yield of the products
questions.C: brings equilibrium faster without shifting its position
questions.explanation: Both directions speed up equally, so the equilibrium mixture is unchanged.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH of a neutral solution at 25°C is
questions.explanation: Pure water has equal H⁺ and OH⁻ concentrations, giving pH 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Dilute hydrochloric acid turns blue litmus paper
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red; alkalis turn red litmus blue.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Phenolphthalein indicator is colourless in acid and turns
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless below about pH 8 and pink in alkaline solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ionic equation for neutralisation is
questions.explanation: Whatever the acid and alkali, the essential change is hydrogen ions meeting hydroxide ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Dilute acid reacts with a metal carbonate to give a salt, water and
questions.explanation: The carbonate fizzes, releasing CO₂ that turns limewater milky.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which acid is dibasic?
questions.explanation: Each H₂SO₄ molecule can release two replaceable hydrogen ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which salt preparation method is suitable for making an INSOLUBLE salt?
questions.C: Neutralising an acid with an alkali
questions.D: Precipitation by mixing two soluble salts
questions.explanation: Mixing two soluble reactants that form an insoluble product precipitates it directly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which compound is deliquescent and is used as a laboratory drying agent?
questions.explanation: Deliquescent substances absorb so much water that they dissolve; CaCl₂ is a classic example.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Washing soda, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, loses its water of crystallisation on exposure to air. Such a salt is
questions.explanation: Efflorescent salts lose their water of crystallisation to the air and become powdery.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A strong acid differs from a weak acid because a strong acid
questions.explanation: Strength is about degree of ionisation, not concentration of the solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water only is called
questions.explanation: Neutralisation removes the acidic and basic properties of the reactants.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which reagent, added to a solution, would confirm the presence of a sulphate ion?
questions.B: Silver nitrate solution in dilute nitric acid
questions.C: Barium chloride acidified with dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.D: Dilute ammonia solution in a test tube
questions.explanation: A white precipitate of barium sulphate that cannot dissolve in acid confirms sulphate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oxidation is the
questions.explanation: Remember OIL RIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the reaction Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, the reducing agent is
questions.explanation: Zinc loses electrons and so reduces the copper ions while itself being oxidised.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of sulphur in SO₂?
questions.explanation: Two oxygens at −2 each give −4, so sulphur must be +4 for the compound to be neutral.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: K is +1 and each O is −2, so Mn = +7 to balance the compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rusting of iron requires both
questions.explanation: Iron rusts only when both air (oxygen) and moisture are present.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Galvanising protects iron from rusting by coating it with
questions.explanation: The zinc layer shields the iron and corrodes sacrificially even when scratched.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Blocks of magnesium are fixed to steel ship hulls to provide
questions.explanation: Magnesium corrodes in place of the iron, protecting the hull sacrificially.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a simple zinc-copper cell, electrons flow through the wire from
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive, releases electrons, and acts as the negative electrode.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When Fe²⁺ changes to Fe³⁺, the iron(II) ion has been
questions.explanation: Losing an electron raises the charge, which is oxidation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of these is an oxidising agent?
questions.explanation: Chlorine readily accepts electrons from other substances.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which metal reacts most vigorously with cold water?
questions.explanation: In the reactivity series, potassium and sodium react violently with cold water.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the blast furnace, the chief reducing agent that converts iron(III) oxide to iron is
questions.explanation: Hot CO from burning coke strips oxygen from the haematite, leaving molten iron.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the blast furnace, limestone is added to
questions.explanation: Limestone decomposes to lime, which combines with sandy impurities to form slag.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aluminium is extracted by the electrolysis of molten alumina rather than by heating with carbon because
questions.A: aluminium is far cheaper than carbon coke
questions.B: aluminium sits too high in the series for carbon reduction
questions.C: alumina melts at a very low temperature
questions.D: carbon reacts violently with hot alumina
questions.explanation: Carbon cannot displace aluminium from its oxide, so electrolysis is required.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Brass is an alloy of copper and
questions.explanation: Brass is copper plus zinc; bronze is copper plus tin.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Stainless steel contains iron with mainly
questions.explanation: Chromium and nickel give stainless steel its rust resistance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When quicklime (calcium oxide) is mixed with water, the product is
questions.explanation: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂, an exothermic slaking reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which metal is found free (native) in the earth's crust?
questions.explanation: Unreactive metals like gold occur uncombined because they are low in the series.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A metal that is liquid at room temperature is
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a flame test, a golden-yellow flame colour indicates the presence of
questions.explanation: Sodium compounds colour the flame golden yellow; potassium gives lilac.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aluminium resists corrosion although it is reactive because
questions.A: a thin oxide film forms on its surface
questions.B: it is covered by oil in the air
questions.C: it does not react with oxygen
questions.explanation: The tough, invisible aluminium oxide layer protects the metal beneath.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which metal is used for making electrical cables because it is a very good conductor?
questions.explanation: Copper combines excellent conductivity with ductility and affordability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Oxygen can be prepared in the laboratory by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. The catalyst used is
questions.explanation: MnO₂ speeds up 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂ at room temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas that relights a glowing splint is
questions.explanation: The glowing splint test is the classic confirmatory test for oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hydrogen gas is prepared in the laboratory by reacting dilute acid with
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂; the gas burns with a squeaky pop.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carbon monoxide is a dangerous gas because it
questions.A: combines with haemoglobin and stops oxygen transport
questions.B: it dissolves the lung tissue slowly in water
questions.C: it turns cold limewater milky white
questions.D: it is a strongly acidic gas in nature
questions.explanation: CO binds haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen does.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carbon dioxide turns limewater
questions.explanation: The cloudy precipitate of calcium carbonate is the test for carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ammonia gas cannot be dried using concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid because
questions.A: ammonia is a base and reacts with the acid
questions.explanation: NH₃ would be neutralised by the acid; it is dried with quicklime instead.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Chlorine gas in the laboratory bleaches damp (not dry) red litmus paper. This shows that chlorine bleaches by
questions.A: forming hypochlorous acid with the moisture
questions.explanation: Chlorine reacts with water to form the bleaching agent HOCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ammonia is manufactured industrially by the
questions.explanation: N₂ and H₂ combine over iron in the Haber process.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The gas that is most soluble in water and gives a fountain experiment in the laboratory is
questions.explanation: Ammonia's extreme solubility sucks water up the tube, producing the fountain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: CFC refrigerants release chlorine atoms that destroy ozone high in the atmosphere.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The general molecular formula of the alkanes is
questions.explanation: Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆ and propane C₃H₈ follow CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The alkene series is described as unsaturated because its members
questions.explanation: The C=C double bond can open up and add other atoms, so the molecule is unsaturated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which compound will decolourise bromine water rapidly?
questions.explanation: Ethene's double bond adds bromine, removing the reagent's colour instantly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many structural isomers does butane, C₄H₁₀, have?
questions.explanation: Butane exists as the straight chain and as 2-methylpropane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Members of the same homologous series have
questions.A: the same general formula and similar properties
questions.B: exactly the same molar mass always
questions.C: the same boiling point for all members
questions.D: different functional groups in the series
questions.explanation: Each member differs from the next by −CH₂−, so properties vary gradually.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanol can be prepared industrially from glucose by the process of
questions.explanation: Yeast converts C₆H₁₂O₆ to ethanol and carbon dioxide at about 35°C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When ethanol is heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ at about 180°C, the organic product is
questions.explanation: Concentrated sulphuric acid dehydrates ethanol, eliminating water to form ethene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to form
questions.explanation: This esterification produces the fruity-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The alkaline hydrolysis of an ester, used in soap making, is called
questions.explanation: Boiling fat with sodium hydroxide gives soap and glycerol: saponification.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Polythene is manufactured by the process of
questions.explanation: Thousands of ethene molecules join to form the long polythene chain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which polymer is formed by condensation polymerisation?
questions.explanation: Nylon forms from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid, releasing water molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Cracking in the petroleum industry means
questions.A: breaking big hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones
questions.B: boiling crude oil into useful fractions
questions.D: burning off the heavy oil residues
questions.explanation: Cracking converts heavy fractions into petrol and useful alkenes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The functional group of the alkanols (alcohols) is
questions.explanation: Alcohols like ethanol and propanol carry the −OH group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Vinegar is a dilute solution of
questions.explanation: Vinegar gets its sour taste and smell from about 5% ethanoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The best method for separating a suspension of chalk in water is
questions.explanation: The insoluble chalk is trapped on the filter paper as the water passes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: To obtain pure water from salt solution, the best method is
questions.explanation: The water vaporises, condenses in the Liebig condenser and is collected pure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Common salt is obtained from its solution by
questions.explanation: The solvent is driven off, leaving the solid salt in the dish.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The separation of pure iodine from a mixture of iodine and sand is best achieved by
questions.explanation: Iodine sublimes on gentle warming and deposits as crystals on a cold surface.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In paper chromatography, the Rf value of a spot equals
questions.A: distance moved by the spot divided by distance moved by the solvent front
questions.B: distance moved by the solvent divided by spot distance
questions.D: the colour intensity of the spot
questions.explanation: Rf values identify substances by comparing how far they travel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Crude oil is separated into fractions such as petrol and kerosene by
questions.explanation: The fractions boil at different temperatures and condense at different levels.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which apparatus is used to deliver an exact volume of 25.0 cm³ of solution in a titration?
questions.explanation: The pipette delivers one fixed volume; the burette measures variable volumes added.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Before smelling an unknown gas in the laboratory, you should
questions.A: waft a little of the gas towards your nose
questions.B: inhale deeply directly from the test tube
questions.C: taste a drop of it on the tongue
questions.D: heat the tube first in a flame
questions.explanation: Wafting limits the amount inhaled in case the gas is irritating or poisonous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which solution is used to test for the presence of chloride ions?
questions.explanation: A white precipitate of silver chloride that darkens in light confirms chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which drying agent is suitable for drying ammonia gas?
questions.explanation: Only a basic drying agent leaves ammonia unreacted; acids absorb it.
